shared_prompt: Wide 16:9 orthographic 2.5D game concept frame of the same cramped British municipal office shown by the references. Preserve the five-room layout and fixed high diagonal camera: front desk at top-left, paper archive at top-centre, money office at top-right, waiting room at bottom-left, weird machine room at bottom-right, and a central corridor. WARM OFFICE / INK BREAK visual language: handmade ink outlines, chunky readable shapes, limited cream, warm plaster, moss, teal, coffee, amber, red and violet palette, shabby wood, scuffed linoleum, paper clutter and fluorescent warmth. Cozy comic bureaucracy, cheap, specific, claustrophobic and lived-in. Clear walkable routes and readable game silhouettes. No glossy corporate lobby, no cyberpunk, no photorealism, no horror dungeon, no random global glitch, no readable text, no logos, no watermark and no large UI panels.

targets.title: CALM OFFICE
targets.prompt: Calm opening state. The teal-coated Warden stands in the central corridor as the primary hero, carrying no folder and facing the current orange-coated customer at the front desk. Runner and Talker are distinct secondary staff. All five room identities read immediately. A few paper folders rest in physical trays; machines are idle but recognizable. Warm lived-in atmosphere, calm short queue, almost no HUD and no chaos.
criteria: Warden is the primary read and the current customer is readable.
Five room identities and walkable routes remain legible.
Paper, folders and machine silhouettes are present without chaos.
Atmosphere feels warm, shabby, specific and lightly funny.

targets.title: AUTOMATION RELIEF
targets.prompt: EDIT REFERENCE IMAGE 1 while keeping its exact outer walls, five-room geometry, fixed high camera and object placement. Repaint the staged machines, folders and staff so they are physically grounded inside the bottom-right Weird Room and fully inherit REFERENCE IMAGE 2's handmade warm-ink linework, scuffed surfaces, three-quarter perspective, shadows, scale and lighting. The squat teal Auto Sorter has folders resting in its input tray and emerging from its output tray; the violet Copy Echo receives them and leaves a small tidy output stack. A staff member physically collects the output. The teal Warden remains elsewhere helping a customer, the queue is short, chairs are empty and the corridor breathes. No cyan route line, no arrows, no connecting path, no floating icons, no boxes, no diagram, no infographic, no HUD and no debug visualization. All cause and relief must exist as ordinary objects and activity in the office.

targets.title: PROMOTION CASCADE BREAK
targets.prompt: EDIT REFERENCE IMAGE 1 while keeping its exact outer walls, five-room geometry, fixed high camera and object placement. Repaint every staged object so it is physically grounded inside the bottom-right Weird Room and fully inherits REFERENCE IMAGE 2's handmade warm-ink linework, worn surfaces, three-quarter perspective, shadows, scale and lighting. The promoted Copy Echo is an oversized red municipal copier standing on the floor; the supervisor stamp is a literal large rubber office stamp mounted on it. Duplicate paper physically spills from the output tray across the room and just through the doorway. Runner physically faces the copier carrying copies. One clean cream original folder with an amber seal lies isolated near the doorway. An actual stop lever, open copy-clear bin and upset customer remain visible and reachable. Thin ink fractures originate in the copier body and continue into the nearby floor and wall. No network lines, no arrows, no circles, no targets, no symbols, no enclosing frame, no floating icons, no diagram, no infographic, no HUD and no debug visualization. The Break must be a local physical office accident, graphic and funny rather than horror.
